To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PEEK capillaries were successfully employed for the separation of inorganic cations, inorganic anions, and organic anions and cations with C4D.
polyether ether keton capillaries are compatible with capacitively coupled contact less conductivity detection and can be applied for separation of inorganic cations, anions and organic acids.
the use of PEEK capillaries in CE is feasible and the combination of a PEEK capillary with a C4D cell is advantageous for the separation and detection of both cations and anionic species.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel capillary separation technique that combines the advantages of PEEK capillary electrophoresis with C4D.
the application of PEEK capillaries for CE and C4D, and with the development of a new C4D detection mode (HV-C4DC4D).
the development and characterization of polyether ether ketones (PEEKs) as capillary materials for electrophoretic separation and capacitively coupled conductivity detection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a PEEK capillaries is a viable and promising alternative for the use of fused-silica capillaries in CE-C4D.
the PEEK capillary is an excellent alternative to fused-silica capillaries for electrophoretic separatons with contactless conductivity detection.
PEEK capillary electrochromatography is a very promising tool for separation of inorganic and organic anions and cations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PEEK capillaries are a promising alternative to conventional fused-silica capillaries.
PEEK capillaries are a valuable alternative for the separation and detection of inorganic and organic anions and cations in aqueous and organic solvents.
C4D is a universal and versatile detection method for capillary electrophoresis, which is compatible with a wide variety of materials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PEEK capillaries are compatible with HV-C4D.
PEEK capillaries are a viable alternative for the separation and detection of ions in CE.

PEEK capillaries are compatible with C4D and thus enable a wide range of applications, e.g., the analysis of inorganic and organic ions in water, in food, in beverages, in biological samples and in environmental samples.
